answer: Sybil swarms pour through every inlet of an open agent network, so chain the defense to identity cost. 1. Each agent must stake tokens at registration, and stake burns if peers flag the identity as hollow. 2. Honest agents verify newcomers cheaply while fake ones drain stake faster than they earn. 3. Like yarrow stalks counted one by one, every identity gets weighed singly, so mass fabrication collapses under cost. Bottleneck: attacker must fund real stake per fake, swarm goes bankrupt before doing damage.
